# C1: Site overview

A table with one row per tower: site ID, name, country, IGBP class, latitude, longitude, first and last year, hub, and the data citation. Most of it is in your snapshot CSV. Add a simple map of the five sites (a world map with five points is enough).

```{r}
## Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

snapshot <- read.csv("data/snapshots/fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261113T105747.csv")

## Create table
five_towers <- c("US-GLE", "BE-Vie", "GF-Guy", "JP-Mse", "AU-Ync")
site_metadata <- snapshot |>
    filter(site_id %in% five_towers) |>
    distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(
    site_id   = site_id,
    name      = site_name,
    igbp      = igbp,
    latitude  = location_lat,
    longitude = location_long,
    hub       = network,
    citation  = product_citation
  )

## Add first / last year per site -------------------------------------------
site_years <- hh_all |>
  mutate(time = as.POSIXct(time, tz = "UTC")) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year  = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Now join, but problem with site Ids in site years
library(stringr)   # for str_split()
site_years <- site_years |>
  mutate(
    site_id = str_split(site, "_", simplify = TRUE)[, 2]   # extract the 2nd token
  ) |>
  # keep only the columns needed for the join
  select(site_id, first_year, last_year)

site_metadata <- site_metadata |>
  left_join(site_years, by = c("site_id" = "site_id")) |>
  # (optional) reorder columns for readability
  select(
    site_id, name, igbp,
    latitude, longitude,
    first_year, last_year,
    hub, citation
  )
```
